clue.text: Waving a flag, ours, bringing one to this mountain

indicators.note: a flag waving flutters about, so the letters of the words that follow are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Patriots wave our banner as they climb, planting it on the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing one to' joins the fodder to the definition: the shuffled letters bring the solver to the mountain, the famous peak over Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugarloaf is the name of a well-known peak, the granite dome above Rio's harbour, so it is an example of a mountain.

clue.text: Southern shopping centre, limited in size

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A shopping precinct in the south is rather cramped.
explanation.definitionFit: Small means of little size, so limited in size is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Reflect it's good to pay attention

parts.note: to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Think it over: it's wise to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflect' suggests thinking but means shine back light.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine with reflected light, as wet surfaces do.

clue.text: Embarrassed, being wrong about hard misleading clue

indicators.note: about means going round, so the two words enclose the letter for hard

parts.note: red-faced with embarrassment
erring means going wrong
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A blushing setter, mistaken, admits a clue was too tough and led solvers astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is something that misleads or distracts, a false lead.

clue.text: Honours cheque, ultimately (indecently large)

parts.note: OBEs are British honours, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of cheque

explanation.surface: Rewards and a payment that is, in the end, obscenely big.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means grossly overweight, so indecently large is a jokey paraphrase.

clue.text: Strange young woman, but musical

parts.note: funny can mean odd or strange
a girl is a young woman

explanation.surface: An odd girl who nonetheless loves to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical' reads as an adjective describing her but is the noun: the stage show about Fanny Brice.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny Girl is a Broadway musical and film about the comedian Fanny Brice.

clue.text: Leader of bunch spots loose broken rock

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so take the start of bunch

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: The chief of a gang picks out a heap of shattered stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' reads as a verb (sees) but is the noun, a skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology brash is a mass of loose broken fragments of rock or ice, a direct dictionary sense.

clue.text: Contralto, yet tenor initially!

parts.note: but and yet both mean however

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of tenor

explanation.surface: A low female voice, but it begins like a tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Clara Butt was a celebrated English contralto of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara Butt was a famous contralto singer, so her name serves as an example of one.

clue.text: A pound, cash thus far

parts.note: L stands for pound sterling, from Latin libra
the ready, or readies, is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: One pound is all the money so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' as slang for cash is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time or up to now, the sense of thus far.

clue.text: Country music down club in America

parts.note: a down is a rolling hill, as in the South Downs of England
a billy club is an American police truncheon

explanation.surface: Folk tunes from the countryside are low in a US nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is not sad but the noun: downs are chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillbilly music was an early name for country music from the rural southern US.

clue.text: Opera song — last part's about a Greek heroine

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: turned about, so the word for the last part is read backwards

parts.note: the end is the last part of anything

explanation.surface: A number from an opera whose final section concerns a woman of Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns END into DNE. Ariadne helped Theseus escape the Minotaur's labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne, daughter of Minos, is a heroine of Greek myth who gave Theseus the thread through the labyrinth.

clue.text: Turning brown — Russian river, as is to be expected

indicators.note: turning the word for brown round means it is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Ural flows from Russia's Ural Mountains to the Caspian

explanation.surface: A Russian river turns brown, which is only what one would predict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning brown' reads as a colour change but reverses TAN to NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something natural is normal and in the ordinary course of things, just what you would expect.

clue.text: Austrian actress on telly ate crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters of the preceding words go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone appearing on television ate some biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits eaten but is slang for mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotte Lenya was a Vienna-born singer and actress, famous in Weill's The Threepenny Opera and in film.

clue.text: Film star getting rid of old clothes

indicators.note: getting rid of means dropping a letter from the star's name

parts.note: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A screen idol throws out her worn-out wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb means clothing, especially distinctive dress, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Member, old fellow, in catastrophic conflict

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member, of the body
aged means old
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A veteran official caught up in a terrible war.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the biblical final battle, so any disastrous all-out war.

clue.text: One giving name inside entrance

indicators.note: inside places the letter for name within the word for entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance to a room or building

explanation.surface: A benefactor writes their name inside the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a person who gives, as of money or blood, so 'one giving' describes them.

clue.text: Hurry on in to stress a point forcibly

parts.note: to drive is to urge or hurry on, as cattle
at home means in, not out

explanation.surface: A speaker races on to hammer an argument home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home is to make it clearly and with force, an idiom.

clue.text: Three of a kind, two of a kind, and a type of flush

parts.note: a pair in cards is two cards of the same rank
a royal flush is the top poker hand, ace to ten in one suit

explanation.surface: A list of poker hands: three of a kind, a pair and a flush.
explanation.walkthrough: A pair royal is an old card-game term (still used in cribbage) for three cards of the same rank.
explanation.definitionFit: In cribbage and older card games a pair royal is a set of three matching cards, three of a kind.

clue.text: Very drunk, father with clarity impaired

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: impaired means damaged, so the letters of clarity are scrambled

explanation.surface: Dad is plastered and cannot think straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Paralytic is British slang for helplessly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Paralytic is informal British slang for extremely drunk, so legless as to be barely able to move.

clue.text: Mostly popular, classes by lake

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
genera are classes in biological classification, plural of genus
L is a standard abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: School classes held beside a lake are usually well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like it qualifies 'popular' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on the whole or usually, so it can stand for mostly in a sentence.

clue.text: Blunder involving Irish beast

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round the abbreviation for Irish

parts.note: a gaffe is a blunder

explanation.surface: A mistake concerning an animal from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe is a tall African animal, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Suitably cast at last in new play

indicators.note: new marks the letters as made fresh, rearranged
at last points to the final letter of cast

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fittingly, the actors are only chosen at the eleventh hour for a fresh drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors but only gives its last letter T, shuffled with PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptly means in a fitting or appropriate way, a direct synonym of suitably.

clue.text: Unfinished article on secret solvent

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
inner can mean private or hidden, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: An incomplete newspaper piece about a hidden chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solvent' could mean able to pay debts, but it is a liquid that dissolves, like paint thinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinner is a liquid solvent used to dilute paint.

clue.text: Take home unopened tea service

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter, the one at the opening, is removed

parts.note: the Royal Navy, RN, is called the Senior Service in Britain

explanation.surface: Bring a tea set home still in its box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea service' reads as a tea set but splits in two: tea loses its first letter, and the Senior Service is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To take home a sum is to receive it as pay, which is what earning means.

clue.text: Foolish and thoughtlessly indifferent group

parts.note: blithe can mean casually careless, showing indifference
a ring is a group of people, such as a spy ring

explanation.surface: A band of people who are silly and couldn't care less.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithering means utterly senseless, as in a blithering idiot.

clue.text: Followed, on the radio, an anthem

indicators.note: on the radio means as it is heard broadcast, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: tracked means followed

explanation.surface: A national anthem was traced by its radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: A tract is a verse sung in the Mass after the gradual in place of the alleluia, a kind of anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: In church music a tract is a chanted passage of psalm verses, a sacred anthem in the liturgy.

clue.text: Naive conservationist

definitions.meaning: a ... is an environmentalist, a member of a ... party

explanation.definitionFit: Green means both untried or inexperienced and concerned with protecting the environment.

clue.text: Sharply curved peak close to Everest

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: close to here means the closing letter of Everest

explanation.surface: A jagged summit near the top of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben is the Scottish word for a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent means curved or crooked, not straight.

clue.text: Not on strike? That's unusual!

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
to beat is to strike

explanation.surface: Workers who are not on strike: how odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but is the verb hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat describes something unconventional or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Musical instruction from an eminent Florentine

parts.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy, was born in Florence

explanation.surface: A conductor's direction coming from a distinguished man of Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a tempo marking on a score telling players to go at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Level before start of throwing competition

parts.note: even means level or flat

indicators.note: the start of throwing is its first letter

explanation.surface: Contestants are level before a shot-put or javelin contest begins.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single contest in a sports programme, such as a field event.

clue.text: Section with a single light out

parts.note: a cut is a section or slice
and means together with
in cricket a single is one run

explanation.surface: Part of a room has one bulb that has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light out' looks like a dead bulb but is slang for leave in a hurry; a single is a cricket term for one run scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To light out is an idiom for leaving quickly, just as cut and run means to flee.
